title: Coconut vegetable korma
description: Cauliflower, potato and peas in a gently spiced coconut and tomato sauce, served with rice.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion with the salt for 7 minutes, stirring until softened.
Add the garlic, ginger and curry powder. Stir for 1 minute, then add the tomatoes, coconut milk, cauliflower and potatoes.
Simmer covered for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the potatoes are tender. Add a splash of water if the sauce becomes too thick.
Stir in the peas and cook for 3 minutes. Squeeze in the lime juice, taste for salt and serve with cooked rice.

tips: Freeze the curry without the rice for up to 3 months.
Use a mild curry powder for a gentler sauce.

title: Lemon salmon with cucumber salsa
description: Golden pan-seared salmon with a crisp cucumber, avocado and lemon salsa.

steps.text: Pat the salmon dry and season with the salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat.
Place the salmon skin-side down and press gently for 20 seconds. Cook for 5 to 6 minutes until the skin is crisp. Turn and cook for another 3 to 5 minutes, until the thickest part reaches 63°C.
Combine the cucumber, avocado and parsley with the zest and juice of half the lemon. Taste and add a pinch of salt if needed.
Divide the salad leaves between plates, add the salmon and spoon over the salsa. Serve with the remaining lemon cut into wedges.

tips: Drying the fish well helps the skin crisp.
Make the salsa just before serving to keep the avocado bright.

title: Blueberry buttermilk pancakes
description: Fluffy pancakes with blueberries, sliced banana and a generous drizzle of maple syrup.

ingredients.preparation: melted, plus more for the pan

steps.text: Whisk together the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt in a large bowl.
Whisk the buttermilk, eggs and melted butter in a separate bowl. Fold the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients just until no dry flour remains; a few lumps are fine.
Heat a lightly buttered skillet over medium heat. Pour in small ladlefuls of batter and scatter a few blueberries over each pancake.
Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until bubbles form and the edges look set. Flip and cook for 1 to 2 minutes more. Repeat with the remaining batter.
Serve warm with banana, the remaining blueberries and maple syrup.

tips: Keep finished pancakes warm in a 100°C oven.
Freeze with baking paper between pancakes and reheat in a toaster.

title: Avocado toast with a crispy fried egg
description: Creamy smashed avocado on sourdough, topped with a crisp-edged egg, lime and chilli flakes.

steps.text: Toast the sourdough until deeply golden.
Mash the avocado with the lime juice and salt, leaving some texture.

Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Crack in the eggs, reduce the heat to medium and fry for 3 to 4 minutes, until the whites are completely set. Cook longer if you prefer a firm yolk.
Spread the avocado over the toast, top each slice with an egg and finish with chilli flakes.

tips: Mash the avocado just before serving.

title: Rainbow chickpea salad with lemon tahini dressing
description: A big, crunchy salad of chickpeas, avocado, radish and colourful vegetables with a creamy lemon dressing.

steps.text: Whisk the tahini, lemon juice, olive oil, maple syrup and salt. Add 3 to 4 tablespoons of water, a little at a time, until pourable.
Arrange the leaves, chickpeas, pepper, tomatoes, carrot, cabbage and radishes in a large bowl.
Add the avocado, drizzle over the dressing and toss gently just before serving.

tips: Keep the dressing and avocado separate if preparing lunches ahead.
The dressing thickens in the fridge; loosen it with a splash of water.

title: Margherita pizza
description: A blistered crust, bright tomato sauce, melting mozzarella and fresh basil. A simple pizza for a very hot oven.

steps.text: Place a heavy baking sheet or pizza stone in the oven and heat to 250°C for at least 30 minutes. Bring refrigerated dough to room temperature while the oven heats.
Mix the tomatoes with the oil and salt. Divide the dough in half and stretch each piece on a floured surface into a 25 cm circle.
Transfer each base to baking paper. Spread with tomato sauce, leaving a 2 cm border, and scatter over the mozzarella.
Slide onto the hot sheet and bake for 10 to 15 minutes, until the crust is deeply golden and the cheese bubbles. Bake separately if needed.
Scatter with basil and serve immediately.

tips: Total time allows for oven preheating; bring cold dough to room temperature first.
Dry mozzarella gives a crisper base.

title: Roasted carrot and ginger soup
description: Velvety roasted carrot soup with fresh ginger, coconut milk and toasted almonds.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C. Toss the carrots with 1 tablespoon of oil and half the salt. Roast for 25 to 30 minutes until tender and browned at the edges.
Meanwhile, heat the remaining oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 8 minutes, then stir in the garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Add the roasted carrots and stock. Bring to a simmer and cook for 5 minutes.
Take off the heat and blend with an immersion blender until smooth. Stir in the coconut milk and remaining salt, then warm gently. Add a splash of water if too thick.
Serve with toasted almonds and coriander.

tips: For a nut-free version, use pumpkin seeds instead of almonds.
Freeze for up to 3 months.

title: Smoky sweetcorn and black bean tacos
description: Warm corn tortillas filled with smoky beans, sweetcorn and crunchy peppers, finished with lime and coriander.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the onion and pepper for 5 minutes.
Add the sweetcorn, beans, paprika, cumin and salt. Cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring, until hot and lightly charred. Add a splash of water if the beans stick.
Warm the tortillas in a dry frying pan for about 20 seconds per side and wrap in a clean tea towel.
Fill the tortillas with the bean mixture and cheese. Finish with coriander, spring onion and a squeeze of lime.

tips: For vegan tacos, leave out the cheese or use a plant-based alternative.
Leftover filling works well in a rice bowl.

title: Brown Butter Banana Bread
description: A moist banana loaf with the nutty flavour of browned butter and a dark, caramelised crust.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 175°C. Grease and line a 23 × 13 cm loaf tin.

Melt the butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Swirl for 4 to 6 minutes, until the milk solids turn golden brown and smell nutty. Pour into a bowl, including the browned bits, and let cool for 5 minutes.
Mash the bananas in a large bowl. Whisk in the sugar, eggs, vanilla and cooled butter.
Mix the flour, bicarbonate of soda, salt and cinnamon separately, then fold into the banana mixture just until combined.
Pour into the tin and bake for 50 to 55 minutes, until a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean. Cover loosely with foil if browning too quickly.
Cool in the tin for 15 minutes, then transfer to a rack. Let cool before slicing.

tips: The bananas should be heavily speckled.
Slice and freeze for up to 3 months.

title: Chocolate chunk cookies with flaky salt
description: Crisp edges, soft centres and generous puddles of dark chocolate. Finish with a little flaky salt.

steps.text: Beat the butter and both sugars until creamy, about 3 minutes. Beat in the egg and vanilla.
Mix the flour, bicarbonate of soda and fine salt, then fold into the butter mixture. Stir in the chocolate.
Scoop into 16 balls. Chill for at least 30 minutes while the oven heats to 180°C. Line two baking sheets.
Arrange the dough balls well apart and sprinkle with flaky salt. Bake for 10 to 12 minutes, until the edges are golden but the centres still look soft.
Leave on the sheets for 10 minutes before transferring to a rack.

tips: Total time includes the 30-minute chill.
Freeze unbaked dough balls; bake from frozen for 2 extra minutes.

title: Little summer berry lattice tarts
description: Buttery individual tarts filled with juicy mixed berries under a golden pastry lattice.

ingredients.preparation: strawberries quartered; other berries left whole

steps.text: Heat the oven to 190°C. Roll two-thirds of the pastry on a floured surface to 3 mm thick. Line six 10 cm tart tins and chill for 15 minutes.
Mix the berries with the caster sugar, cornflour and lemon zest. Divide between the pastry cases.
Roll the remaining pastry and cut into thin strips. Weave a loose lattice over each tart, pressing the edges to seal. Brush with beaten egg and sprinkle with demerara sugar.
Bake on a tray for 25 to 30 minutes, until the pastry is golden and the filling bubbles. Cool for at least 20 minutes before removing from the tins.

tips: Total time includes chilling the pastry; cool for at least 20 minutes before serving.
Put the tins on a tray to catch any bubbling berry juice.

title: Seeded wholemeal bread rolls
description: Hearty wholemeal rolls with a soft crumb and a generous coating of sunflower, pumpkin and sesame seeds.

steps.text: Mix both flours with the yeast and salt. Add the oil and water, then mix to a rough dough.
Knead on a lightly floured surface for 10 minutes, until smooth and elastic. Place in an oiled bowl, cover and leave for 60 to 90 minutes until doubled.
Divide into 8 equal pieces and shape into rolls. Brush the tops with water and press into the seeds. Arrange on a lined tray, cover loosely and prove for 30 to 45 minutes until puffy.
Heat the oven to 220°C. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until well browned and hollow-sounding when tapped underneath. Cool on a rack.

tips: Allow 90 to 135 minutes for rising; total time uses a 2-hour rise.
Freeze cooled rolls, then reheat from frozen at 180°C for 10 minutes.

title: Chocolate brownie milkshake
description: A thick chocolate shake with whipped cream, chocolate sauce and a bite of brownie on top.

steps.text: Chill two serving glasses in the freezer for 5 minutes.
Whip the cream to soft peaks. Drizzle half the chocolate sauce around the inside of the glasses.
Blend the ice cream, milk and remaining chocolate sauce until thick and smooth. Add a splash more milk if needed.
Pour into the glasses. Top with whipped cream and a piece of brownie, then serve immediately.

tips: Use cold glasses and very cold milk for a thicker shake.

title: Miso ramen with salmon and soft-boiled eggs
description: A quick miso broth with springy noodles, seared salmon, jammy eggs and plenty of spring onion.

steps.text: Bring a small pan of water to a boil. Lower in the eggs and cook for 7 minutes. Transfer to cold water, then peel and halve.
Pat the salmon dry. Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and sear the salmon for 4 minutes on the first side and 3 to 5 on the second, until the thickest part reaches 63°C.
Simmer the stock with the ginger for 5 minutes. Meanwhile, cook the noodles according to the packet directions and drain.
Turn off the heat under the stock. Mix the miso with a ladleful of hot stock, then stir back into the pan with the soy sauce.
Divide the noodles between bowls, pour over the broth and top with salmon, eggs, spring onions and sesame seeds.

tips: Add the miso off the heat to keep its flavour bright.
For firm egg yolks, boil for 10 minutes instead.

title: Crispy oven fries with parmesan and parsley
description: Golden oven-baked potato fries with crisp edges, grated parmesan and fresh parsley.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 230°C with two large baking sheets inside. Cut the potatoes into 1 cm fries, leaving the skins on if you like.
Rinse the fries in cold water and dry thoroughly with a clean tea towel.
Toss with the oil and salt. Spread carefully over the hot trays in a single layer with space between them.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, turning after 20 minutes and swapping the trays, until deeply golden. Scatter with grated cheese and parsley and serve hot.

tips: Dry potatoes and space on the tray make the biggest difference to crispness.

title: Steak and mushroom tagliatelle
description: Seared steak, golden mushrooms and cherry tomatoes tossed with ribbons of pasta in a light cream sauce.

steps.text: Pat the steak dry and season with half the salt and all the pepper. Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large skillet over high heat. Sear the steak for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until cooked to your preference. Transfer to a board and rest for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the tagliatelle in salted boiling water according to the packet. Reserve a mug of cooking water before draining.
Add the remaining oil to the skillet. Cook the mushrooms over medium-high heat for 5 minutes until golden. Add the tomatoes, garlic and remaining salt and cook for 3 minutes.
Reduce the heat and add the cream and spinach. Simmer for 2 minutes, until the spinach wilts.
Slice the rested steak thinly. Toss the pasta into the sauce with a splash of cooking water, then fold in the steak and its resting juices. Serve immediately.

tips: Slice steak across the grain to keep it tender.

title: Cucumber mint cooler
description: A crisp, gently sweet sparkling cooler with fresh cucumber, mint and lime.

steps.text: Reserve a few cucumber slices and mint sprigs for garnish. Put the remaining cucumber, mint, lime juice and sugar in a small jug.
Press gently with a wooden spoon to release the cucumber juice and mint aroma. Stir until the sugar dissolves.
Fill two tall glasses with ice. Divide the cucumber mixture between them, top up with sparkling water and stir gently.
Garnish with the reserved cucumber and mint. Serve straight away.

tips: Add the sparkling water just before serving to keep the bubbles.
Gently press the mint rather than crushing it to a paste.

title: Hibiscus iced tea with lemon
description: A ruby-red hibiscus infusion with a bright squeeze of lemon, brewed as a jug for the fridge.

steps.text: Bring the litre of water to a boil in a saucepan. Turn off the heat, add the hibiscus and cover. Steep for 10 minutes.
Strain through a fine sieve into a heatproof jug. Stir in the sugar while the infusion is warm, then add the cold water.
Allow to cool for 20 minutes, then refrigerate for at least 40 minutes until cold.
Stir in the lemon juice. Taste and dilute with a little extra cold water if too tart. Serve over ice with lemon slices.

tips: Total time includes steeping and cooling.
Keep covered in the fridge for up to 3 days; add ice only when serving.

title: Strawberry lemonade
description: Fresh strawberries and sharp lemon juice blended into a bright pink lemonade for sharing.

steps.text: Blend the strawberries, lemon juice, sugar and 250 ml of the water until smooth and the sugar has dissolved.
For a smoother drink, pour through a fine sieve into a jug. Stir in the remaining 500 ml of water.
Taste and add a little extra water or sugar if needed. Fill four glasses with ice and pour over the lemonade.
Garnish with lemon slices and mint, then serve.

tips: Refrigerate the lemonade for up to 2 days and stir before pouring.
Frozen strawberries work too; thaw them before blending.

title: Vanilla iced coffee
description: Strong chilled coffee over plenty of ice, softened with oat milk and a little vanilla syrup.

steps.text: Stir the maple syrup and vanilla into the chilled coffee until combined.
Fill two glasses with ice and divide the coffee between them.
Pour in the oat milk, stir and taste. Add a little more maple syrup if you like it sweeter. Serve immediately.

tips: Prep and total times assume the coffee is already chilled.
Freeze leftover coffee in an ice cube tray to chill the drink without diluting it.

title: Ginger lime spritz
description: A lively alcohol-free spritz made with fresh ginger syrup, lime and sparkling water.

steps.text: Put the ginger, sugar and water in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Remove from the heat and let the syrup steep and cool for 20 minutes. Strain into a small jug and discard the ginger.
Fill four glasses with ice. Divide the ginger syrup and lime juice between them.
Top each glass with sparkling water, stir gently and garnish with lime slices and mint. Serve straight away.

tips: Total time includes cooling the syrup.
Make the syrup up to a week ahead and refrigerate in a clean covered jar. Add sparkling water when serving.
